traces.description: Fixed boss-actor WRAM flag inputs observed at call sites; each helper masks the literal input to its low three bits.
traces.method: Each candidate pairs the immediate `LDA` input with its `TestWramFlag_Offset100` call; the helper masks the input with `$0007` and adds `$0100`.
The spawned actor parameter is decoded by the actor engine, then the actor-specific caller transform and helper offset select the index.

traces.description: Possible event-flag indices selected by spawned Diamond Mine laborer actor parameters and the actor's lookup table.
traces.method: Only rows for `dm3F_laborer` actually spawned in `scene_actors.asm` are included. The actor parameter decodes to the byte-table X index; `extracted/diamond_mine/mine_main/dm3F_laborer.asm` uses that index to select a flag byte from `extracted/diamond_mine/mine_main/dm3F_laborer.asm`, then calls `TestFlagRaw / SetFlagRaw`. Unspawned entries in the actor's local table are excluded.

traces.description: Possible event-flag indices selected from the statue-reward table.
traces.method: The selected four-byte `statue-reward` row supplies the raw event-flag index to the claim test and flag set.
assumptions: system/statue_inventory/statue_inventory_reward.asm: statue-reward entry +0 is the raw event-flag index (TestFlagRaw / SetFlagRaw)

traces.description: Possible event-flag indices used for per-scene enemy-clear reward/reveal state.
traces.method: The helper adds `$0300` to a scene index; nonzero table rows bound scenes with configured enemy-clear reward behavior.
assumptions: tables/enemy_clear_reward_table.asm: one tier byte per scene id (row position = scene id), nonzero = reward configured

traces.description: WRAM indices selected by the matched boss-reward range row.
traces.method: The caller matches the current scene to a boss-reward row; its row number is masked to 0-7 before `$0100` is added.
assumptions: actors/boss_clear_reward_handler.asm: BossRewardFindScene takes the first row whose scene id matches; row number masked to 3 bits by the helper

traces.description: Possible event-flag indices referenced by table-driven barrier and chest records.
traces.method: The callers read the fourth record byte, mask it to seven bits, and pass it to the `$0200` helper.
assumptions: tables/scene_chest_table.asm: chest-entry byte 3, bits 0-6 = flag; callers mask with $7F then the helper adds $0200

traces.description: Event flags used to guard enemy death actions; zero-valued death-action indices are skipped by callers.
traces.method: Enemy-spawn rows supply the death-action index, actor execution stores it, and the helper adds `$0100`.
assumptions: scene_actors.asm enemy-spawn rows: operand 7 (event-block index) is the death-action index; zero = no flag

traces.description: Possible WRAM indices set when a nonzero enemy number is defeated and tested to suppress defeated enemies on later scene loads.
traces.method: Enemy-spawn rows supply the enemy number; actor execution stores it, the dungeon-kill COP handler passes it directly to `SetWramFlag`, and scene loading tests the same index in `wramFlags`.
assumptions: scene_actors.asm enemy-spawn rows: operand 6 (enemy number) is the wramFlags index; zero = no flag

traces.description: Status-menu ability flags computed from the current character form and selected ability slot.
assumptions: system/inventory/inventory_menu.asm: slots 0,1,2 from the immediates before TestAbilityFlag (the status cursor $22 walks the same rows 0-2)

traces.description: Flag index of every `$13 branch` command in the scene_meta command streams (runtime operand of SceneCmd_Branch).
traces.method: `SceneCmd_Branch` reads its flag index with `ReadScriptByte` and calls `TestFlagRaw`; every operand sits in a literal `branch < flag, label >` command of `tables/scene_meta.asm`, decoded record by record (replaces the old unresolved input `SceneCmd_ConditionalLoad`).
assumptions: tables/scene_meta.asm: the scenes of a candidate are the scene ids that reach the branch (linear flow, jump and set-branch follow the label)

traces.description: The offset WRAM helper family can address exactly indices `$0100-$0107` after masking its input.
traces.method: Helper implementation masks the caller value with `$0007`, then adds `$0100`.
